source_files: coverage.csv, sources.json and gaps_by_state.md from the 2026-11-07 case law access survey. The survey opened public court and library web pages and read what they said; it logged in nowhere and used no CourtListener key. Court sites change, so treat every row as a place to start looking.

legend.CAP: Harvard's Caselaw Access Project: a free bulk copy of reported (published) opinions that ends between 2008 and 2019, depending on the state
legend.Scholar: Google Scholar case law (web search only)
legend.JS: needs JavaScript, which the survey's automated check could not run

status.accessible: the survey could open the page
status.partial: only part of it could be read
status.blocked: the survey's automated check was refused, or the site disallows automated readers; it may still open in your own browser
status.unknown: not checked, or the survey could not tell

basis.observed: the survey read the start year on the page
basis.inferred: the survey worked the start year out from what it could see

sources.access_method: bulk (CSV bz2 snapshots on public S3; aws s3 --no-sign-request)
sources.cost: free (opinions file 55.3 GB, clusters 2.5 GB, dockets 5.1 GB at 2026-09-30)

sources.access_method: bulk (per-reporter/volume JSON+HTML on static host; metadata JSON)

sources.cost: $0.10/page, $3 cap per document, fees waived if <= $30/quarter; 'Court opinions are always free' (observed)

sources.access_method: web search; API (token); dockets bulk CSV
sources.auth: none for web; token for API
